summary: Lambek's decision procedure for the product-free Lambek calculus of Lambek.v: a bottom-up search for a cut-free derivation, bounded by the number of connectives. The search is proved sound and complete, so derivability, with or without cut, is decidable. Computed examples include two balanced sequents that the count invariant cannot reject.

sources.citation: Lambek, J. (1958). The mathematics of sentence structure. Amer. Math. Monthly 65(3):154-170.
Moot, R. & Retoré, C. (2012). The Logic of Categorial Grammars. LNCS 6850. Ch. 2-3.

definitions_mapped.note: fuel-bounded boolean search over the axiom, the right rule and every left rule at every position

theorems.name: splits_spec
theorems.source_claim: added: the enumeration of the ways to cut a list in two is correct

theorems.name: holes_spec
theorems.source_claim: added: the enumeration of the positions in a list is correct

theorems.name: prove_sound
theorems.source_claim: Lambek 1958 §8: every sequent the search accepts is cut-free derivable

theorems.name: prove_complete
theorems.source_claim: Lambek 1958 §8: every cut-free derivable sequent is accepted once the fuel exceeds its connective count

theorems.name: derivable_b_spec
theorems.source_claim: Lambek 1958 §8; M&R Prop 2.18: the bounded search decides derivability with cut

theorems.name: walks_john_rejected
theorems.source_claim: illustration: np\s, np does not derive s; beyond the count invariant

theorems.name: type_raising
theorems.source_claim: M&R p. 30; Lambek 1958 §7: np derives s/(np\s)

theorems.name: raised_not_lowered
theorems.source_claim: M&R p. 45: s/(n\s) does not derive n; balanced

theorems.name: a_very_book_rejected
theorems.source_claim: M&R §2.5 p. 33: the empty-antecedent restriction rejects np/n, (n/n)/(n/n), n

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
Soundness and completeness are stated against cf_derivable and Deriv of Lambek.v, and decidability with cut uses that file's cut elimination (derivable_iff_cf).
The search returns a boolean, not a derivation; the file says so and gives no complexity bound.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. The procedure is Lambek's, with fuel as the decreasing argument. Atom equality is a hypothesis of the section.

artifact_classes.description: the search is a fuel-bounded boolean function, not a derivation-producing procedure
splits and holes of a list enumerate the rule positions
